## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement rotation using only shifts and masks, handling edge cases without branches.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and masking
- Modulo arithmetic for 32-bit width
- UB avoidance for shifts by 32

## Code Example
```javascript
// C-like signature
uint32_t rotr32(uint32_t n, unsigned r) {
  r &= 31;
  return (n >> r) | (n << ((32 - r) & 31));
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of cross-lane bit manipulation and wrap-around across a 128-bit value.

## Key Concepts
- 128-bit split across two uint64 halves
- Cross-lane bit movement with shifts
- Non-branching bitwise updates

## Code Example

uint128 rotateLeft128_1(uint128 x) {
  uint64_t new_lo = (x.lo << 1) | (x.hi >> 63);
  uint64_t new_hi = (x.hi << 1) | (x.lo >> 63);
  uint128 r; r.hi = new_hi; r.lo = new_lo; return r;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests precise bit manipulations without branches, a common need in codecs and bitboards.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and masks
- Rotation vs simple shift
- Handling 0-31 safely without undefined behavior

## Code Example
```c
uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t x, unsigned k){
    k &= 31;
    return (x << k) | (x >> ((32 - k) & 31));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- What happens for k=0 or k=31? Explain results and edge handling.
- How to generalize to 64-bit values? Discuss performance trade-offs and compiler optimizations.
